title: Why tigers are orange, not green

scenes.headline: Why is a forest hunter bright orange?
Because its prey can't see orange.
scenes.body: Deer have two-colour vision. To them, a tiger's orange blends into green.
scenes.source: Fennell et al. 2019, J. R. Soc. Interface

scenes.headline: A neural network searched for the best tiger colour.
scenes.body: Seen through deer-like eyes, orange hid the tiger as well as green would.
scenes.source: Fennell et al. 2019, J. R. Soc. Interface

scenes.headline: And mammals can't grow green fur.
scenes.body: So orange is the best camouflage a tiger can actually make.

caption:
Tigers are orange because their prey sees orange as green.

In tests with people, an orange-red target was much easier to spot in images simulating three-colour vision than in images simulating two-colour vision.

Sources: Fennell J.G. et al. (2019) J. R. Soc. Interface 16:20190183; University of Bristol. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Answers a question viewers never thought to ask with a 2019 study, so the payoff feels earned; no fake 'deer-vision' filter is shown.
